title: Al-Qawiyy, the Strong
tomorrow: strength runs out. what kind doesn't?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Al-Wakil, the Trustee, the one you hand a worry to. The line: entrusted. Some days, though, the worry can't be handed off. It has to be lifted.
screen: `ENTRUSTED.` → `AND WHEN IT HAS TO BE LIFTED?`

segments.voice: New town. No job, no friends, no idea where you'll sleep tonight. And the one thing you need, water, has a crowd around it that won't let anyone weak get near. That's where Moses is. He has fled Egypt with nothing. He reaches a well in Midian, and the shepherds are shoving their flocks to the front. Off to one side, two young women hold their sheep back and wait. He asks why. They tell him they can't water until the shepherds are done, and their father is a very old man. So Moses walks into the crowd.
screen: `NEW TOWN, NOTHING IN YOUR POCKETS.` → `A WELL, AND A SHOVING CROWD.` → `MOSES WALKS IN.`

segments.voice: He waters their flock for them. Then he does something the hero of a movie never does. He walks off into the shade, sits down, and says, in Pickthall's translation: "My Lord! I am needy of whatever good Thou sendest down for me." A minute after the strongest moment in the scene, the strong man says out loud that he's empty. Later one of the women tells her father: "O my father! Hire him! For the best (man) that thou canst hire is the strong, the trustworthy." She saw both, the arms at the well and the man in the shade. Today's Name is Al-Qawiyy, the Strong. Muslims keep a short phrase for heavy days that hands strength back to where it comes from: la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, there is no power and no strength except with Allah. The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, called it a treasure from the treasures of Paradise. Notice what the phrase doesn't say. It doesn't say you're weak, or that you should sit still. Moses still hauled the water. It says the strength was lent. And here's the detail worth telling a friend tonight: in this story, the prayer for help comes after the strong act, not instead of it.
screen: `HE WATERS, THEN SITS IN THE SHADE.` · `I AM NEEDY OF WHATEVER GOOD.` · `THE STRONG, THE TRUSTWORTHY.` · `NO STRENGTH EXCEPT WITH ALLAH.` · then, large: `HIS STRENGTH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing this week that feels heavier than you are: a test, a talk you're dreading, someone you're caring for. On each slow out-breath, say quietly la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah, or in English, no strength except with God. If the words aren't yours, let the breath itself do the saying, and let the weight be shared for two minutes.
screen: `ONE HEAVY THING.` · `NO STRENGTH EXCEPT WITH GOD.`

segments.voice: Al-Qawiyy. The Strong: the Name behind the arms at the well, and behind the man in the shade who asked.
Keep this one close: his strength, lent to you for the bucket, the hill and the hard talk. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Muslims often say la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah when facing something heavy, and call on Allah as Al-Qawiyy, the Strong, in personal du'a.

fork.setup: your friend carried the whole group project. afterward she tells you, quietly, that she's running on empty. what does the well in Midian say about her?
options: a real leader keeps that to herself until it's over.
she did the strong thing, and saying she's empty is part of it.
she should have asked for help instead of doing the work.
fork.reveal: Moses watered the flock, then said "I am needy of whatever good Thou sendest." the story keeps both: the strong act and the honest ask.

original.note: Arabic: the Strong. it shares a root with quwwa, the strength in la hawla wa la quwwata.

trapdoor: what you thought: God as the strongest one in the room.
what it means: all strength is His, and what you have is lent, so you use it and still ask.

chat.says: dadi's knee surgery is tomorrow. dad said 'you're the strong one.' i'm honestly terrified. now what?
options: Be strong and scared. Moses did the hard part, then sat down and asked for help.
Hide the fear. Being the strong one means dad never sees you shaky.
Tell dad to pick someone else. Strength is a gift, and you just don't have it.
chat.meaning: Moses watered the flock, then said he was needy. The strength is lent: la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah.
